recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No core follow-up is needed for FHIR-35972 unless a future work group decision changes the multiple-specimen Observation modeling pattern.
issue_request: FHIR-35972 was Published as Persuasive for R5 and requested adding Specimen to Group.member.entity so multiple-specimen Observation workflows could reference a Group, preferably with a restriction to specimen-only groups when used for Observation specimens.
initial_application: The Jira comment cites commit 7816ce80374c4e5d31d1a5cb48b80b0701744337, and git history confirms that commit added the Specimen target profile to Group.member.entity. The current combined source still contains that target profile and the specimen Group.type code.
additional_context: Group is active in source/fhir.ini. Related FHIR-34002 added Reference(Group) and the obs-9 invariant on Observation.specimen requiring referenced Group members to resolve to Specimen. OO and FHIR-I minutes support this split between Group-side target support and Observation-specific restriction. Later FHIR-39269 decided to retain Specimen in Group and explain the Observation compatibility rationale, while later FHIR-52918 broadened other Group member types without removing Specimen.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current active source already satisfies the seed request: Group.member.entity allows Specimen, group-type includes specimen, Group.type requires consistency with member types, and Observation.specimen carries the context-specific specimen-only Group invariant.

related_jiras.note: Observation multiple-specimen issue that added Reference(Group) to Observation.specimen and the specimen-only Group invariant; already represented on the combined branch.
Later Published decision rejected removing Specimen from Group and added narrative explaining why Specimen remains; already represented on the combined branch.
Later Applied Group issue broadened other member types and Group.type wording while retaining Specimen support; already represented on the combined branch.
